description: Machine-readable schema for the EMP Knowledge Graph and Engram memory store. Companion to week2_memory_architecture.tex. Grounded in real output from CodeGraph (codegraph status / codegraph explore) and Engram's actual mem_save / memory_relations schema, plus the real hoangnb24/repository-harness structure.

implementation_scope.description: Release 0.1 implements only the capabilities listed as supported. node_kinds and edge_types remain the forward-looking EMP vocabulary and are not a guarantee that every capability is extracted today.

node_kinds.description: A standalone function definition
An import statement, as its own node (not just an edge); resolves separately to its target file/module
A function attached to a struct/class/interface
A struct (Go-style; closest equivalent to a class in some languages)
A named constant value
A source file
One value inside an enum
A significant module/package-level variable
A web-framework route, linked to its handler function via a REFERENCES edge
An interface/protocol definition
An enum type
A type alias
A named property on a type
A class definition (non-Go languages)
A trait definition (Rust)
A named exception/error type that can be raised (e.g. InvalidPasswordError); not itself a code symbol CodeGraph extracts as a node today, but referenced by THROWS edges
A database table name referenced in a query; not itself a code symbol CodeGraph extracts as a node today, but referenced by QUERIES edges
A docs/stories/*.md story packet; a committed, re-derivable artifact linked to the functions/files it touched
A docs/decisions/*.md committed decision record, indexed as a graph node; its content is additionally mirrored into Engram as a decision-type memory (see split_rule.decisions_refinement)

A section extracted from general project documentation (README, architecture notes, design docs) -- one per H2 heading. Broader and less structured than decision_ref (no required Status/Consequences fields).

edge_types.name: DEFINES
edge_types.meaning: The file's own body contains this symbol's definition.

edge_types.name: IMPORTS
edge_types.meaning: The file contains an import statement; the Import node then resolves separately to its target file/module.

edge_types.name: CALLS
edge_types.meaning: The source function's body directly invokes the target. One hop only; multi-hop paths are computed at query time via traversal, not pre-stored.

edge_types.name: THROWS
edge_types.meaning: The function's body contains a raise/throw statement for this exception type, directly (not via a called function).

edge_types.name: QUERIES
edge_types.meaning: The function executes a read/write against this database table.

edge_types.name: ROUTE_HANDLER
edge_types.meaning: A detected framework route (e.g. an HTTP endpoint) is bound to its handler function.

edge_types.name: REFERENCES
edge_types.source: file | function | method | variable | constant | property
edge_types.meaning: The source symbol's body reads or otherwise uses the target symbol, without calling it as a function (e.g. reading a module-level constant, referencing another variable).

edge_types.name: TESTS
edge_types.meaning: A test function or method directly exercises (calls and asserts against) the target function or method's behavior.

edge_types.name: AFFECTS
edge_types.target: file | function | method | class | struct | interface | trait | enum | route
edge_types.meaning: The decision or story's content names/references this code element, indicating the decision explains why it exists or was built this way.

edge_types.name: CONTAINS
edge_types.source: file | function | method | class | struct | interface | trait | enum
edge_types.target: function | method | struct | class | interface | trait | enum | import | variable | constant | property | type_alias | route
edge_types.meaning: The file's own body contains this symbol -- CodeGraph's general containment relationship, broader than DEFINES (which only covers callable/type declarations).

edge_types.name: INSTANTIATES
edge_types.meaning: The function's body creates an instance of this class/struct (e.g. `new Foo()`).

record_schema.title: Short, searchable, verb + what (e.g. 'Chose Zustand over Redux')
record_schema.topic_key: Stable key for an evolving topic (e.g. 'architecture/auth-model'); reused to update rather than duplicate a memory

content.Why: What motivated it (bug, request, performance, etc.)
content.Learned: Gotchas or edge cases (omitted if none)

memory_relations_schema.id: INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT â€” local autoincrement key; excluded from sync payloads as it is not cross-machine portable
memory_relations_schema.sync_id: Unique id for this relation row (TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE)
memory_relations_schema.relation: The relation type (TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'pending')
memory_relations_schema.marked_by_model: Model that asserted it, if applicable
memory_relations_schema.superseded_at: TEXT â€” timestamp when this relation was superseded by another; NULL if active
memory_relations_schema.superseded_by_relation_id: INTEGER REFERENCES memory_relations(id) ON DELETE SET NULL â€” points to the replacement row when superseded

split_rule.rule: If a fact can be regenerated by re-parsing the current source code, it belongs in the Knowledge Graph. If it requires knowing history or reasoning that no longer exists in the code, it belongs in Engram as a memory record, optionally linked to graph nodes via a memory_relations-style verified edge.

examples.fact: We chose JWT over sessions for horizontal scaling
examples.why: reasoning, not present in the code

examples.fact: This bug was caused by a race condition in session refresh

split_rule.decisions_refinement: docs/decisions/*.md files are committed and versioned, making them re-derivable (Knowledge Graph material by the letter of the rule), but their content is exactly what Engram is meant to hold. Resolution: index the file as a Knowledge Graph 'decision_ref' node (it is a real, linkable artifact), and additionally mirror its content into Engram as a 'decision'-type memory record for full-text search and memory-relation verification. The split rule decides where a fact's source of truth lives, not where it may also be indexed for retrieval.

structure.AGENTS.md: Stable agent shim: local notes + links to docs below (not itself a rules file)
structure.docs/product/: Current product contract, derived from a spec
structure.docs/stories/: Story packets: units of reviewable work
structure.docs/decisions/: Durable decisions and tradeoffs, committed to the repo

extraction_spec.extracted_as: Risk classification rules; read once per session to tag incoming work; not stored as graph/memory data itself
Declared module boundaries; cross-checked against CodeGraph's actual import/call edges to flag boundary violations
Behavior-to-proof mapping; linked to route and function nodes it covers
Knowledge Graph 'story' node, linked to the functions/files it touched
Knowledge Graph 'decision_ref' node + mirrored Engram 'decision'-type memory record (see split_rule.decisions_refinement)

storage_decision.technology: SQLite with FTS5 full-text search, for both the Knowledge Graph and Engram
storage_decision.rationale: Both reference implementations (Engram, CodeGraph) independently converge on this stack. Avoids introducing a separate graph database server (e.g. Neo4j); WAL mode ensures concurrent reads are never blocked by an in-progress write; FTS5 provides full-text search over both code artifacts and memory records natively.
